title: Review concierge docket — quick hypotheses & preflight notes
body:
Purpose: quick personal docket for the PRs I'm reviewing this sprint. Mix of micro-checks, hypotheses to validate during review, and explicit follow-ups so I don't lose context when switching tasks. Mostly shorthand notes to self and a few things to ask the author in-thread.

PRs on my plate:
- PR #4987: runtime: compact-kv-cache fallback + config flag (Maya)
  quick impression: small surface change but touches cache invalidation path. tests added but only unit-level.
  risks: stale cache on multi-worker rollout; potential perf regression for short sequence workloads.
  preflight checks:
    * trace a failing scenario locally (sequence lens 8–16) with 8 concurrent requests — watch hit/miss ratio.
    * confirm metrics emitted: kv_cache.evictions, kv_cache.hit_ratio, kv_cache.prefix_misses
    * ensure cache key format hasn't changed across rollouts (old format -> new format): quickly grep for key serializer.
  quick repro notes (local):
    1) run ./scripts/run_local_infer.sh --model tiny --seq 16 --concurrency 8
    2) env REDWOOD_CACHE_DEBUG=1 make test-infer  # watch logs for "kv-cache: miss"
  questions for author: did you consider TTL vs explicit invalidation? if TTL chosen, why 5m default?
  follow-ups: add a canary load test in staging (see linked PR).

- PR #5021: console: rollout UI for canary/AB targeting (Omar)
  quick impression: mostly UI + a thin API surface. Concerned about the API contract ambiguity (targeting rules schema).
  preflight checks:
    * validate schema in frontend and backend types (TypeScript types vs Go structs) — run type generation script.
    * check rollout fallback if rule parse fails: should default to safe route (old model)
  todo: propose small CI step to validate sample targeting configs as JSON schema.

Micro-review heuristics I ran through (for small PRs):
- Does it change request/response contract? if yes, add migration note + integration test that asserts old clients are not broken.
- Is there any implicit cross-service behavior (cache keys, metrics, tracing tags)? add explicit unit to assert tag names.
- Any new config flags? Document default values and rationale in the flag comment and PR description.
- Perf-sensitive path: add a rough opcount check (hot loop allocations) or a flamegraph note.

Refactor idea seed (low-cost experiments):
- Normalize cache key building into a single helper that accepts context + model-id + seq-range. Replace ad-hoc builders in 3 places. Rationale: reduces rollout surface and makes A/B of key formats easier.
- Small adapter layer for rollout rules: backend returns a stable "route-id" for a request. Let console and routing both interpret this, instead of each parsing rules independently.

Rollback & emergency playbook notes (reminders to myself):
- If kv-cache regression: immediate mitigation is to set REDWOOD_CACHE_MODE=legacy on Dedicated nodes via feature-gate (ops runbook RT-33).
- If canary UI causes broken routing schema: disable console rollout feature flag from admin UI and revert PR-5021. Keep a short revert template ready: one-liner revert PR with "revert: revert of PR-xxxx (reason)".
- Always collect a 1-minute flamegraph and the top 10 traces (trace ids saved in the rollback ticket).

Testing checklist (fast local + CI):
- unit tests cover edge-case false positives for cache key equality
- small e2e: 20 requests with mixed prefixes to assert expected hit ratio delta
- load: smoke run with concurrency 16 to catch allocator regressions

Notes-to-self:
- avoid leaving TODOs without ticket numbers in PRs. If a TODO is non-trivial, open a Linear and link it under "linked_artifacts".
- prefer small follow-up PRs for refactors (makes rollbacks easier).

Conversation snippets to paste into review thread:
- "Flagged the potential stale-cache scenario above — can you add a short note on invalidation strategy? If TTL, let's document the choice (perf vs freshness) and the default value tradeoffs."
- "Looks good overall; small nits inline. Can we add a one-sentence rationale for the schema change to the PR description so we have historical context?"

Open questions (unresolved):
- Is the default 5m TTL globally appropriate or should it be model-specific? (need perf numbers per model family)
- Should rollout rule evaluation be last-writer-wins or prioritized rule-sets? (tradeoffs for predictability vs expressivity)

Next actionable items (today):
- run the local kv-cache trace for PR-4987, collect hit/miss data (30m)
- leave inline comment on PR-5021 about schema validation and propose JSON schema in a follow-up
- if both look good, queue a staging canary for tomorrow and add canary checklist to the rollout ticket.

Random personal heuristics (for review speed):
- If a PR touches < 200 lines and has a clear unit test delta, do a shallow + focused review (20–30m).
- If it touches infra/serving/runtime assumptions, escalate to pair review and schedule 30m sync.

End of docket.

-- rhea
